correctness.rationale: In a connected complete multipartite graph, total domination is equivalent to meeting at least two parts. Therefore support at least three is automatically secure under any legal one-vertex exchange. With support exactly \(\{i,j\}\), an omitted vertex in part \(i\) can only be defended from \(j\); after the exchange two parts remain represented exactly when \(s_i=n_i\) or \(s_j\ge2\), and symmetrically for \(j\). Subtracting the two one-defender obstruction families from all subsets meeting at least two parts, with their one-one intersection restored, gives the displayed polynomial. A fresh direct brute-force replay on representative multipartite profiles matched the criterion for every subset.

value.rationale: Secure total domination is a standard robustness variant, and complete multipartite graphs are a canonical family. The theorem gives the exact feasible-set structure and all-cardinality polynomial, from which the minimum parameter follows immediately. This is a natural enumerative refinement rather than a routine recomputation of a known minimum.
